Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the AetherCloud Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to register by pressing star one one on your telephone keypad followed by your name and affiliation. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Chen, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Chen:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing AetherCloud's results for the Q3 2024. With me on the call are Mike Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Kline, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Product Officer; Taylor Brooks, Chief Marketing Officer; Chris Patel, Chief Sales Officer; and Lisa Chen, Chief Security Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Rivera.

Mike Rivera:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. AetherCloud continued its strong growth trajectory in the Q3, driven by robust demand for our comprehensive suite of cloud services and solutions.

During the quarter, our key priorities included:
1. Expanding our presence in emerging markets.
2. Accelerating the adoption of our AI-powered platform.
3. Enhancing our developer ecosystem.
4. Strengthening our commitment to sustainability.
5. Investing in employee training and development.
6. Improving cross-functional collaboration.
7. Ensuring the security and privacy of our customers' data.

Enterprise customers and large deals were standout highlights this quarter, forming the bedrock of our business. Enterprise now accounts for 68% of our total remaining performance obligations, or RPO, at quarter-end, up from 64% a year ago. This shift reflects industries moving toward mission-critical cloud workloads, especially AI/ML inference at scale, sovereign data residency solutions, and hybrid multi-cloud setups.

We closed 47 deals with annual contract values over $10 million—a 32% year-over-year increase and our best quarter yet for these mega-deals. Among them, 12 were $50 million-plus ACV multi-year commitments, totaling more than $3.2 billion in total contract value, or TCV. Current RPO from these wins grew 28% year-over-year to $18.7 billion, while future RPO jumped 41% to $12.4 billion, highlighting the long-term nature of these agreements. Net retention stayed strong at 128%, with 62% of our top 500 customers expanding their compute and storage usage by an average of 2.7 times.

Key wins included three net-new Fortune 100 customers. A global financial services leader on the scale of JPMorgan Chase chose AetherCloud as their primary public cloud for core banking modernization in a $180 million TCV, five-year deal. This involves migrating legacy mainframe workloads to our Kubernetes-orchestrated AetherKube platform, integrated with our GenAI Inference Engine on NVIDIA H100 GPUs. They're using our serverless AetherLambda for real-time fraud detection at sub-50ms latency across petabyte-scale data lakes. We won after outperforming Azure with 25% lower effective pricing on sustained-use commitments and better data retention.

A pharmaceutical powerhouse like Pfizer signed a $125 million TCV for sovereign cloud in EMEA, deploying AetherSovereign zones in Frankfurt and Paris for clinical trial data pipelines. Integrated with Snowflake for federated analytics, it offers HIPAA-level security via AMD SEV-SNP enclaves, displacing on-prem HPC and speeding drug discovery AI by 4x with our AetherAI Fabric scaling across over 10,000 GPUs.

In manufacturing, an automotive OEM akin to Volkswagen Group committed $95 million TCV for digital twin simulations on AetherIoT Edge, processing 5TB/hour of factory sensor data into physics-informed neural networks on AetherML. This expands a pilot and taps our 150% year-over-year growth in manufacturing ACV.

We also deepened ties with existing clients. A retailer like Walmart upsold $220 million TCV for e-commerce personalization, shifting from GCP to AetherCommerce with Pinecone vector search. An energy supermajor resembling ExxonMobil renewed and expanded for $150 million in seismic processing on AetherHPC, using custom Trainium2 silicon for 40% cost savings over rival TPUs.

Driving this are three trends: AI workloads in 71% of large deals, up from 45% last year, favoring inference with our AetherAI Fabric's 3.5x performance edge over AWS Inferentia; multi-cloud and sovereignty surges, with 67% growth in sovereign deals after launching zones in Mumbai, São Paulo, and Sydney for 22% APAC hyperscale share; and sustainability, where 40% of deals highlighted our 100% renewable matching and carbon-aware scheduling for 28% TCO cuts.

Regionally, North America took 55% of large deal value at $2.1 billion TCV, EMEA 25% at $950 million with 45% growth, APAC 15% at $575 million up 60% ex-China, and LATAM 5% at $200 million. We displaced AWS in 18 deals, Azure in 12, and GCP in 8, often on price-performance and egress-free networking.

Our land-and-expand strategy shines, with 84% expansions from customers over $5 million prior spend. Sales pipeline is $42 billion, up 35% year-over-year, 62% enterprise-weighted, with 41% win rates on $10 million-plus deals versus Gartner's 28% industry average.

For Q4, we expect $4.5-5 billion in large deal TCV, backed by $2 billion FY25 capex for Trainium3 and Nitro 6 instances plus 20 new edge locations. Enterprise growth of 25-30% into FY25 outpaces IDC's 22% cloud forecast.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Kline to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Sarah Kline:
Thank you, Mike. We are pleased to report another quarter of strong financial results. Revenue grew by 25% year-over-year to $28.5 billion, exceeding our guidance. Our gross margin was 72%, reflecting our efficient cost structure. Our operating margin was 32%.

Good afternoon, everyone—thank you for joining AetherCloud's Q3 2024 earnings call. I'll walk you through our key infrastructure metrics, focusing on compute and storage capacity utilization rates. These metrics highlight our operational efficiency and demand elasticity in the hyperscale cloud space, as we monetize our global data centers amid AI/ML surges, enterprise migrations, and edge growth.

Globally, compute utilization averaged 84% in Q3, up 450 basis points quarter-over-quarter and 12% year-over-year—our highest since Q4 2022. This was propelled by 28% year-over-year growth in GPU-accelerated instances like Aether Graviton4 and Aether Inferentia2 for large language model training, serving partners of OpenAI and Anthropic. CPU-only held at 79%, while HPC and GPU clusters reached 92%, showing AI outpacing traditional loads.

Storage utilization hit 78%, up 380 basis points quarter-over-quarter and 9% year-over-year. Aether Object Lake led at 82% for data lakehouses and IoT/video analytics; block storage for databases/VMs at 74%; archival at 62% via intelligent tiering.

Trends show AI inference/fine-tuning at 35% of compute hours, up from 22%, with 95th percentile hourly utilization over 91% in North America. Legacy VMs stabilized, offset by spot instances at 18% capacity with 65% discounts. Hot storage grew 31% year-over-year, compressing cold tiers.

Regionally: North America at 88% compute/83% storage, boosted by Oracle/VMware escapes; EMEA 81%/76% with sovereign uptake; APAC 79%/72%, Mumbai at 65% in first 90 days; LatAm/MEASA at 71%/68%.

Initiatives include Aether Capacity Optimizer using ML forecasting to cut idle capacity 22% quarter-over-quarter. Custom ARM Graviton4 is 15% of fleet for 30% better price-performance. Erasure-coded storage cuts rebuilds 40%, enabling 85% raw utilization.

We're balancing supply with 62% Reserved Instance coverage locking $18 billion backlog, PUE at 1.18 with 45% renewables. Q4 guide: 85-87% compute, 79-81% storage, with AI upside.

These rates affirm our demand-led expansion, funding innovation beyond commoditized IaaS.

Next, I'd like to introduce Dr. Elena Vasquez, who will provide an update on our technology roadmap.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Sarah. We are making significant investments in research and development to stay at the forefront of cloud innovation. We are particularly excited about our progress in network performance and reliability.

Good afternoon, everyone. Before deeper tech details, let's highlight our network moat—crucial for mission-critical workloads like AI clusters and trading platforms. Customers demand four- to five-nines availability, sub-10ms latencies, and minimal outages.

In Q3, we hit 99.999% monthly uptime across 42 Availability Zones—five nines, beating our 99.99% SLA and AWS's 99.98%. That's 26 seconds unplanned downtime per month per instance, down 40% year-over-year. Trailing 12-month: 99.9995%, top of Synergy's index.

Performance: 7.2ms P99 end-to-end latency globally, down 18% year-over-year via Anycast and load balancing. Inter-region throughput over 150 Tbps peak, packet loss <0.0005%, jitter <1ms P95, retransmissions at 0.001%.

Regionally: North America 99.9998% uptime/5.8ms latency (52% workload); EMEA 99.9992%/9.1ms with EU Edge Network; APAC 99.998%/8.5ms despite cables; LATAM/India 99.997%/12ms with new peering.

Backed by $450 million FY24 CapEx: NexusGuard AI predicts 92% incidents, MTTR under 4 minutes; SDN with EVPN-VXLAN for 60% faster convergence; 12,000km fiber including trans-Pacific.

This drives NPS to 78, 97.5% retention, $2.1 billion net new ARR from migrations. Targeting six nines by FY25 end with quantum-safe and satellite backhaul—every 0.01% gain boosts contracts 2-3%.

Now, I'll pass it to Jordan Lee for a product update.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Elena. We recently launched AetherAI Fusion, which is already gaining significant traction in the market.

Good morning, everyone. Let's discuss our new service launches and strong market reception amid AI, edge, and sustainability shifts. IDC forecasts $1.4 trillion cloud spend in 2025, 21% CAGR, 30% AI-driven—we're leading.

AetherAI Fusion, our serverless AI inference platform on NitroHypervisor, cuts latency 40% versus GPU clusters, supports TensorFlow/PyTorch/Hugging Face with NVIDIA H100/Blackwell for 2.5x throughput on Llama 3/AetherGPT.

In four months, 2,500 customers (320% QoQ), including streaming for 15PB transcoding (35% TCO cut vs. Azure) and healthcare for 1.2M inferences/hour. $180 million new ARR, $1.2 billion RPO up 45%, NPS 78.

EdgeForge Network expanded to 120 locations for 5G IoT/AR/VR, with Knative/eBPF. Automotive OEM for 50,000 vehicles cut egress 28%. Bookings 210% YoY, 18% edge share, $95 million revenue, 72% margins on Graviton4.

North America 62% uptake; EMEA 150% YoY with EU AI Act; APAC 280%; LATAM 110% on carbon-aware scheduling.

AetherConnect enables multi-cloud, FinOps saves 22%. Q4 QuantumShield for confidential AI. Expect $500 million ARR add.

I'll now hand it over to Taylor Brooks to discuss our marketing strategy.

Taylor Brooks:
Thank you, Jordan. Our marketing efforts are focused on building brand awareness and generating demand for our solutions.

Today, I'd like to highlight our cost optimization initiatives and their impact, key to our financial discipline in a competitive market where AWS has 31%, Azure 25%, Google 12% share per Synergy—we hold 8% IaaS/PaaS.

These delivered $650 million annualized savings year-to-date, expanding non-GAAP operating margins 420 bps to 28.7%.

Infrastructure: PUE to 1.12 via liquid immersion in Virginia/Frankfurt, saving $180 million on energy; 35% ARM silicon fleet cuts compute costs 17% YoY.

Workload rightsizing via FinOps/Kubecost automated 70% workloads, saving $210 million; renegotiated NAND/DRAM for 15% lower pricing; 62% Reserved Capacity at 65% discounts.

Nimbus Optimizer AI forecasts 92% accurately, cuts idle 31% ($140 million); spot orchestration for sub-50% costs.

North America 20% reductions funding expansions; APAC 16% via edge PUE<1.10; EMEA 11% on renewables, saving $45 million.

Savings fund R&D like Nitro Enclaves/EKS Anywhere; customer FinOps adoption up 45%, net retention 118%. FY25: 10-15% cost compression, FCF $1.8 billion TTM up 35%.

Next, I'd like to introduce Chris Patel, who will provide an update on our sales performance.

Chris Patel:
Thank you, Taylor. Our sales team delivered a strong performance in the Q3, driven by increased customer adoption of our cloud services.

Good afternoon. Before sales specifics, our revenue guidance for Q1 FY2025 and full year reflects execution as #2 provider, 28% AI inference share.

Q1 FY2025 revenue: $28.2-28.8 billion, 24-27% YoY from $22.7 billion.

Segments: IaaS/Storage $14.5-14.9 billion (26-29%), Graviton4 ramp; PaaS/Data $8.1-8.4 billion (25-30%), ForgeML/EKS; SaaS/Emerging $5.5-5.6 billion (18-21%), sovereign/serverless.

ARR $112 billion (+23%), RPO $180 billion (+35%), NRR 118%.

Regions: Americas $15.5-15.9 billion (25%); EMEA $7.1-7.3 billion (26%); APAC $5.6 billion (28%).

CapEx $4.5 billion for Inferno TPUs, renewables PUE 1.10, Outposts growth, DataSphere acquisition. Op income $10.8-11.2 billion, FCF $9.5 billion.

Risks: FX, antitrust, non-AI softness—but margins cushion.

Finally, I'll pass it to Lisa Chen to discuss our security initiatives.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Chris. Security is our top priority. We are committed to protecting our customers' data and maintaining the highest standards of security.

Good afternoon. Our security and compliance certifications are a key differentiator, fueling 28% enterprise growth and $1.2 billion new ARR in regulated sectors.

Achieved FedRAMP High for Core/Kubernetes, passing 421 NIST controls for DoD IL5, winning at 20-30% lower TCO.

ISO 27001:2022 for Frankfurt/Paris with Schreiner, GDPR enhancements via Compliance Copilot—35% EU fintech uptick.

IRAP PROTECTED in Australia for Sydney/Melbourne, 42% ANZ growth.

HITRUST CSF r2 perfect score for HIPAA; PCI DSS 4.0 full scope; SOC 2 Type II with Deloitte, remediation <48 hours.

Certified services 72% of $8.7 billion revenue, 95% renewals vs. 85% avg. $250 million R&D for zero-trust, quantum-safe, anomaly detection (2.7M threats, MTTR 14 min).

Multi-cloud Fabric CNCF-conformant. Pursuing CCCS Canada, FedRAMP AI. Underpins 32% FY24 growth to $36 billion.

Back to Mike Rivera.

Mike Rivera:
Thank you, everyone. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, we will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Ben Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Mike, with AI workloads exploding, how sustainable is the enterprise momentum, especially given macro headwinds?

Mike Rivera:
Thanks, Ben. Sustainability comes from our flywheel—high net retention at 128%, pipeline up 35% to $42 billion, and AI in 71% of deals. Enterprise stickiness with 97% gross retention mitigates discretionary risks. We're positioned for 25-30% growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong:
Great, thanks. Sarah, can you expand on the Q1 guidance assumptions, particularly around margins and capex?

Sarah Kline:
Absolutely, Lisa. Guidance assumes continued AI at 32% mix, with op margins at 38% from efficiencies like PUE 1.10 and ARM shifts. Capex $4.5 billion skewed to AI silicon, but utilization 85-87% supports FCF $9.5 billion. Balanced across regions.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Raj Patel:
Thanks. Elena, on the tech side, how do network reliability gains support new AI services, and any updates on quantum initiatives?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Good question, Raj. Five-nines uptime and 7.2ms latency enable AetherAI Fusion's low-latency inference, with NexusGuard predicting issues for <4 min MTTR. Quantum-safe pilots for FY25 six-nines, integrated with satellite backhaul for edge AI resilience.

Mike Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. We appreciate your continued support.

Alex Chen:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
